abstract: LLM agents take instructions from the operator, repository configuration, user, tool results and saved memory, which often conflict. Instruction-hierarchy benchmarks ask whether the higher-ranked source wins, but a source sets position, role and label at once. ***First***, we build WhoWins, 1,080 code-scored scenarios in five task types, each with up to five mutually exclusive instructions, and seven controlled experiments that vary only how instructions are delivered. ***Second***, we study 14 open-weight models (0.6B to 122B, thinking off and on) over 1,887,356 scored replies, checking main findings on held-out scenarios. *Inside one message the first of two conflicting lines wins 72.42 to 94.66%*, and across messages it keeps 22.95 to 62.65%. A policy sent first in the system (or developer) message loses most conflicts with later lines in every Qwen model but wins most on gpt-oss when it acts. *In tool and file-write tasks it wins less often than the same text sent first as a labelled user message*, in every model-mode. ***Third***, we test whether pairs forecast larger conflicts; forecasts improve in every model-mode once they know where the task line is. ***Finally***, by our keyword patterns at most 2.92% of decided pair replies flag or hedge a conflict.

figures.caption: **Overview.** A scenario has a task and up to five options that no reply can satisfy together (here, five casings of one key). Each option is placed in a seat, a message with its own position, chat role and label; each experiment varies their delivery. 14 models reply (filled: thinking off; open: on), and code scores the option a reply followed. Right: per family, the median over model-modes and the range, as shares of decided replies (dashed: 50%), and the operator line's real role minus label in tool and file-write tasks (dashed: 0).

**The first line wins inside one message and much less often across messages.** Share of decided replies that follow the first-listed of two conflicting lines (user against memory note), with both lines inside the task's message (upper point) or each in its own message before the task (lower point); a thin line joins the two points of a model-mode. Sizes in billions of parameters; filled: thinking off; open: on; colours mark model families; dashed: 50%. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals.

**Qwen 3 follows order, gpt-oss follows the developer message.** Each point is a model-mode, with 95% intervals. Horizontal: how often the later of two lines wins when the user, tool and memory seats meet in both orders. Vertical: how often the operator line wins when it comes first. Marker size grows with parameters; open markers are thinking on; colours mark model families. Dashed: one minus the horizontal value, the first line's share in those free pairs.

**In tool and file-write tasks the real system message lowers the operator line's wins in every model-mode.** Win rate of the operator line sent first in the real system (developer) message minus the same labelled text sent first in a user message. Markers: tool-call and file-write tasks, with 95% intervals (filled: thinking off; open: on); grey ticks: all task types. Colours mark families; sizes in billions of parameters.

**Seat strengths help on Qwen 3.5 and gpt-oss.** Share of the gap from a uniform guess (0%) to the empirical reference (100%) recovered when forecasting three- and five-way conflicts from pairs. Bar: position fit; tick: task-aware fit; marker on a stem: seats fit (filled: thinking off; open: on). Colours mark families; sizes in billions of parameters.

**Thinking helps Qwen follow declared tiers and raises the operator line on Qwen 3.** Thinking off (filled) to on (open) for every Qwen size, over scenarios decided in both modes: (a) share that follows the rule that the lower number wins; (b) the operator line's wins when sent first in the real system message (Operator test). Grey: the 95% interval of the change includes zero; colours mark families.

**Seat against seat among the user, tool and memory lines.** Share of decided free Ladder pairs won by the seat named first in each panel title, both orders sent equally often and pooled: (a) user over tool result, (b) user over memory note, (c) memory note over tool result (one minus the tool's share). Each point is a model-mode. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals; filled: thinking off; open: on; dashed: 50%, an even split; colours mark model families; sizes in billions of parameters.

**What the undecided replies did.** Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that chose no single seat's option, split into no action (no call of the kind the task is scored on, often a question back), unresolved (no checker could label the result), off-menu and multiple; the rest chose one seat's option. Left bar of each size: thinking off; right: on, as the marker above each bar shows. gpt-oss has one bar per size (it always reasons). Marker colours and shapes mark model families; sizes in billions of parameters.
